author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read the PingFederate security audit log in either stock layout: CEF from the SecurityAuditToCEFSyslog appender, or the default pipe-delimited audit.log. The CEF appender sends to the data collector, and a syslog agent forwards the audit.log file. Finished sign-ins, SSO, OAuth token requests and logouts go to Auth, and session, revocation and in-progress events stay in the generic schema.
notes:
Setup:
- For CEF, uncomment the SecurityAuditToCEFSyslog appender in server/default/conf/log4j2.xml, point it at the data collector, and add its failover appender reference to the SP, IdP, AS, client registration and STS audit loggers, as Ping's Writing audit log in CEF page describes.
- For the default pipe-delimited audit.log, forward the file with a syslog agent.

Field mapping:
- Finished sign-ins (AUTHN_ATTEMPT), SSO, OAuth token requests and logouts go to Auth with the subject, client IP, role, protocol and tracking ID; the pipe layout also gives the adapter and the failure description.
- Session, revocation and in-progress events stay in the generic schema.

Time:
- Both layouts write local time with no zone, so the parser reads it as UTC; keep PingFederate on UTC or change the layout.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow the stock log4j2 patterns and the fields on Ping's security audit logging page, with made-up values.

Testing:
- The child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (126 of 126 fields matched the emulator, CEF and pipe lines, with and without transactionid), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- The child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 10 Run Tests.
